name: continuum
author: Smealm
description: Bridges Flashpoint Infinity and Flashpoint Ultimate: uses Infinity's own on-demand sources to cache the whole archive in the background, resumably and with a disk-space guard.

continuum.manager.title: Continuum Manager
continuum.manager.description: Status, estimates, disk space and download controls in one place.

continuum.progress.title: Check Ongoing Progress
continuum.progress.description: See the current catalogue rebuild or download with a live progress bar. Closing the window does not stop the job.

continuum.startActive.title: Start Active Download
continuum.startActive.description: Download at full speed with all workers. Confirms size and free disk space before starting.

continuum.startPassive.title: Start Passive Download
continuum.startPassive.description: Download slowly in the background with a single worker and pauses between games.

continuum.pause.title: Pause Downloads
continuum.pause.description: Finish the current game, then stop. Progress is saved and resumes later.

continuum.rescan.title: Rebuild Catalogue
continuum.rescan.description: Re-read every game from the launcher database (about a minute with the fast build). Needed after metadata updates or to notice files added outside Continuum.

continuum.fastCatalogue.title: Fast Catalogue Build
continuum.fastCatalogue.description: Read the launcher database directly with a sqlite3 tool, instead of asking the launcher for every tag. About a minute instead of hours, and identical results. The tool is looked for in the Flashpoint folder and on PATH, and is checked before it is used. Falls back to the tag scan when no working tool or database is available.

continuum.sqlitePath.title: SQLite Tool Path
continuum.sqlitePath.description: Optional. Full path to a sqlite3 program, for a system where none is found (macOS usually has /usr/bin/sqlite3; many Linux installs do not). Relative paths are read from the Flashpoint folder. A tool path here is tried before the Flashpoint folder and PATH.

continuum.mode.title: Download Mode
continuum.mode.description: The mode the manager's Start button uses. Passive uses one worker and pauses between games, for a mirror that runs in the background. Active uses the configured workers at full speed. The separate Start Active and Start Passive buttons still choose explicitly, and a resumed job keeps its saved mode.

continuum.scope.title: Download Scope
continuum.scope.description: What to mirror. Use the value field below to name the platform, tag, library or playlist.

continuum.scopeValue.title: Scope Value
continuum.scopeValue.description: Platform (Flash, HTML5), tag (Puzzle), library name or playlist title. Ignored when scope is all.

continuum.reserveGB.title: Keep Free Disk Space (GB)
continuum.reserveGB.description: Continuum pauses before free space drops below this. It warns instead of filling the drive.

continuum.maxTotalGB.title: Download Limit (GB)
continuum.maxTotalGB.description: Stop after this much data in the current job. 0 means no limit.

continuum.activeWorkers.title: Active Workers
continuum.activeWorkers.description: The most parallel downloads active mode may use. This is a hard ceiling: with adaptive parallelism on, Continuum starts at two and raises the count until the download is pressing the best speed the connection has shown. Keep it modest; the archive servers are shared.

continuum.adaptiveWorkers.title: Adaptive Parallelism
continuum.adaptiveWorkers.description: Measure the best speed the connection delivers and use as many parallel downloads as it takes to reach it, up to the Active Workers ceiling. To learn that speed before the queue reaches a large game, a job runs one 30-second probe of a large pack at most once an hour, discarding the bytes; only adaptive active jobs do this. Within 10% of the measured peak the worker count holds, a wider width that delivers less is dropped, and server failures halve it.

continuum.order.title: Download Order
continuum.order.description: Smallest games first sorts the whole catalogue by remaining bytes and finishes far more playable games in the same total time, because the archive's sizes are heavily skewed. Total mirror time is unchanged; the big games simply arrive last. Playlist priority still wins over this. Catalogue order keeps the old sequence.

continuum.passiveWorkers.title: Passive Workers
continuum.passiveWorkers.description: Parallel game downloads in passive mode. Adaptive parallelism is off in passive mode; this is the exact number used.

continuum.passiveDelayMs.title: Passive Delay (ms)
continuum.passiveDelayMs.description: Pause after each game in passive mode.

continuum.respectFlashpointSettings.title: Respect Flashpoint Settings
continuum.respectFlashpointSettings.description: Follow the launcher's own preferences: skip extreme-rated games when its extreme filter is on, request compressed images when it caches compressed images, and skip logos and screenshots when its image caching is off. Switch this off to ignore all three: no extreme filtering, images always uncompressed, and images cached even if the launcher's image caching is off. Turn image caching off in the launcher, with this switch on, to skip images; Continuum has no separate switch for that.

continuum.autoMirror.title: Keep The Mirror Current Automatically
continuum.autoMirror.description: On launcher start, continue an unfinished job. While the launcher is open, rebuild the catalogue when its database changes and download only the games that rebuild changed. Start a fresh pass when something in scope is still missing and no job is saved. Automatic jobs run in passive mode; a resumed job keeps the mode you started it with. Replaces "Resume On Launcher Startup".

continuum.prioritizePlaylists.title: Playlist Games First
continuum.prioritizePlaylists.description: Pull games from your playlists to the front of the download queue. Everything is still downloaded; playlist games just arrive sooner. Checked while running: adding a game to a playlist moves it ahead of the remaining queue, and switching this off stops new moves without losing progress.
